effect_definition: |beta_pollinator| - |beta_plant|, days per degree C; negative = plant more temperature-sensitive, positive = pollinator more temperature-sensitive

ecological_result.source_backed_spatial_reversal: Xie 2022 reports flowering more temperature-sensitive in warmer regions but bee phenology more responsive in colder regions.
ecological_result.licensed_summary: Local plant-pollinator partners commonly differ in thermal phenological sensitivity, but which partner is more responsive is system- and geography-dependent. Shared local environmental access does not guarantee matched or consistently ordered climate responses.

paper2_decision.reason: A formal E7 pooled effect would require either unreported cross-model covariance assumptions or mixing noncommensurate phenophase/synchrony estimands.

prohibited_claims: the diagnostic pooled mean is a valid E7 meta-analytic estimate
plants universally track warming faster than pollinators
pollinators universally track warming faster than plants
local-versus-migrant taxon identity causally explains information-distance effects
natural information hysteresis has been observed
